name: Emerging-market stress
value: Lira, Egyptian pound at record lows
summary: Turkish lira and Egyptian pound at record lows; no major EM default or capital controls
state: The Turkish lira hit a new record low on 4 Nov, near 50 per dollar, in a gradual slide (Izvestia; Benzinga). Egypt's pound passed 56 per dollar in late October, a record low, as foreign funds sold local debt (Reuters via MarketScreener). Neither has lost more than 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy had defaulted or imposed capital controls as of 4 Nov.
for_you: Travellers and importers dealing in these currencies face shifting exchange rates. No acute emerging-market crisis is under way.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month; no default or capital controls = Normal

sources.title: Izvestia — Turkish lira reaches new historical low
MarketScreener (Reuters) — Egypt's currency hits record low of 56 pounds

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
